feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 3 (±0.08 m, 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint, track 0.12) removed s-bend and slalom line loss (0.6 and 0.95 down to 0), but the oval finish rate fell to 45%. Iteration 4 (track 0.10, body 0.12, mass 0.7) raised the oval finish rate to 65% with oval oscillation 0.174, but the s-bend and slalom still ended off_track at max_error about 0.062 with progress 0.127 and 0.093. The limit is now turn response, not sensing. Decide the next change from the race. If the s-bend or slalom still end off_track at max_error near 0.06 m with progress not improving, keep the 0.09 m track and try a lighter body, for example body_length 0.10 m, rather than further narrowing. If s-bend progress falls below 0.127 or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25, the turn gain is overshooting, so return wheel_track to 0.10 m and reduce sensor lead by moving sensor y to 0.03 m. If the oval finish rate falls below 55% while line loss stays at zero, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep the lighter mass.
requested_changes: If s-bend progress falls below 0.127 or oval steering_oscillation rises above 0.25 at wheel_track 0.09 m, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and move sensor y from 0.05 to 0.03 with x fixed. If the s-bend or slalom still end off_track at max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.3 at track 0.09 m, keep the track and try body_length 0.10 m with mass 0.5 kg, leaving the sensor array fixed. Evidence: iteration 4 (track 0.10, mass 0.7) still had max_error 0.062 and progress 0.127 and 0.093, so the chassis needs to be lighter and shorter.

If the oval finish rate falls below 55% with line loss still at zero, return wheel_track to 0.10 m and keep mass at 0.6 kg. Evidence: track 0.10 gave a 65% oval finish rate in iteration 4, while track 0.12 gave 45% in iteration 3 with the same sensor array.
